_comment: Regression corpus for splitIntoSentences(). Fields: [lang, input, expectedCount, note].
These lock in BEHAVIOUR THAT WAS VALIDATED AGAINST REAL BOOKS, not idealised
linguistics. Several cases assert a deliberate trade-off rather than a
'correct' answer -- notably the ordinal and single-initial rules, which stop
'15. Januar' and 'Dr. Meyer' from splitting at the cost of also not splitting
a sentence that genuinely ends in a number or a one-letter token. Those
trade-offs were chosen because the false splits were far more common and far
more damaging in the source texts than the missed ones.
Counts are UNIT counts. A bracket whose contents contain a complete sentence is
lifted out of the sentence carrying it: the surrounding text rejoins into one
unit, and the footnote's own sentences become units of their own -- so such a
case yields MORE units than the visible sentence count suggests.
Cases tagged TRADE-OFF assert a deliberate compromise rather than a 'correct'
answer. If you change the splitter and one of those flips, read the note before
updating the number -- it may be a fix rather than a regression.
cases: Das ist ein Satz. Das ist ein zweiter Satz.
Er kam am 3. Januar an. Dann fuhr er weiter.
ordinal inside a date must not split
Der Text steht auf S. 42. Der Text geht weiter.
TRADE-OFF: ordinal rule also suppresses a real break after a number
Vgl. dazu Dr. Meyer und andere. Der Text geht weiter.
closing quote glued to the terminal punctuation
repeated terminal punctuation is one break
literal three-dot ellipsis before lowercase does not split
the U+2026 glyph behaves identically to the three-dot form
an ellipsis before an uppercase word still ends the sentence
Ein Satz [mit einer Fußnote. Und noch einer.] geht weiter.
bracket ends with a complete sentence -> lifted out; main text rejoins into one unit
Ein Satz [mit einer Fußnote. Und noch einer] geht weiter.
bracket trailing off mid-clause is a gloss, not a footnote, even though a sentence ends inside it
Er war [wo sie wohnten, als Heyking 1885 stellvertr. Generalkonsul war] dort.
an unlisted abbreviation inside a gloss must not get it lifted out
von Herrn von Seldeneck [deutscher Ministerresident in Chile] vom Schiff abgeholt. Ende.
inline gloss mid-sentence, real break after it
Wir kamen an. [Fußnote: Am 4. April 1886 kam er. Er reiste ab.] Weiter.
a footnote block at a sentence boundary IS split into its own sentences
Text [Fußnote: siehe Meyer.] Und weiter. Ende.
contents decide, not position: one complete sentence inside is enough to lift it out
Ein Satz endet. [Fußnote: siehe Meyer.] Und weiter.
same bracket at a sentence boundary behaves the same way
Ein Gedanke — plötzlich — kam ihm. Er blieb.
isolated em dashes do not break
Am 1. 1. 1900 begann es. Danach kam nichts.
This is a sentence. This is another one.
Prof. Smith arrived late. He apologised.
a quoted exclamation followed by lowercase does not end the sentence
»Ihr habt das Korn teuer gemacht, gebt uns zu essen!«, was sich darauf bezog.
a comma after the closing quote means the clause continues
ellipsis before an uppercase word does split
C'est une phrase. En voici une autre.
Il est arrivé en retard. Personne ne savait.
Esta es una frase. Y esta es otra.
Questa è una frase. Eccone un'altra.
Dit is een zin. Dit is een tweede zin.
Esta é uma frase. E esta é outra.
Gallia est omnis divisa in partes tres. Quarum unam incolunt Belgae.
One sentence here. Another sentence there.
